title: Guest Meals Taken Out of the Allowance Pot
content:
Guests brought to the counter on an Employee Meal Account reduce the pot the employee's own ticket may draw on.

**Clause.** Where the plan allows guest meals and two or more guest meals have been rung on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the amount taken out for guest meals is the whole value of those guest meals, since a run of them exhausts what the employer funds. Where the plan allows guest meals and exactly one guest meal has been rung on the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the amount taken out is the guest surcharge printed against the plan, once. Where neither holds, nothing is taken out for guest meals.

## The plan figures this reads

| Meal plan | Guest meals allowed | Guest surcharge printed against the plan |
|---|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | no | $0.00 |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | yes | $4.50 |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | yes | $4.50 |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | yes | $5.25 |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | no | $0.00 |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | yes | $12.00 |

## The bands

| Plan allows guest meals | Guest meals rung in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | Taken out of the pot |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 2 or more | The whole value of those guest meals |
| Yes | Exactly 1 | The guest surcharge printed against the plan, once |
| Yes | None | Nothing |
| No | Any | Nothing |

Note the difference between the two bands: on a run of guest meals it is their whole value that leaves the pot, while on a single guest meal it is only the printed surcharge.

*Hypothetical illustration.* On a plan printing a $5.25 guest surcharge, 3 guest meals in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked worth $41.00 together take $41.00 out of the pot; one guest meal worth $14.00 in that month takes $5.25 out.
